From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: DPA clarifications and data handling (Acme Payments)

Hi Lydia

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand Acme Payments' integration plans. Quick recap and the items you asked us to clarify regarding data handling and the DPA: 

1) Controller/Processor roles: Acme will be the controller and Redwood the processor for any customer-provided payment PII sent to our inference endpoints. We have that relationship reflected in the DPA (see Section 2).

2) Subprocessors: You requested the current subprocessors list and our onboarding/removal process. Attached: subprocessors-list.csv. We notify customers 30 days in advance for material changes and provide an opt-out path for sensitive regions.

3) Data retention & logging: By default we retain request/response logs for 30 days for debugging and billing; retention can be configured by customers on Dedicated/Private tiers. We store only minimal request metadata beyond that period unless you opt-in for longer retention for audit purposes.

4) Breach notice & response SLAs: We commit to 72-hour initial notification for confirmed incidents affecting customer data, and a full incident report within 30 days.

Attached is the DPA draft I promised (Redwood-DPA-v3.pdf). Can you confirm which sections you want redlined? Specific asks from your side — e.g., stricter residency, retention limits, subprocessors exclusions — will help us prioritize legal review.

Next steps:
- Please flag any DPA redlines by EOD Wednesday (your timezone).
- If you want, I can loop in our security lead (Marissa) for a brief call to walk through the subprocessors list and breach procedures.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Ben — thanks for the recap and for sending the DPA. A few questions from our security/legal team that I need clarified before we circulate redlines: 

- Controller/Processor: We understand our position as controller and Redwood as processor. Can you confirm whether Redwood will ever act as a joint-controller for derived data or aggregated analytics? If so, what data elements are used and how is consent handled?

- Subprocessors: The CSV is helpful. For subprocessors processing EU data specifically, can you confirm whether subprocessors are limited to EU-hosted vendors or if you use US-based analytics vendors that may access logs?

- Breach notice timing: You mentioned 72-hour notification — is that 72 hours from detection or from confirmation? We typically require 24 hours from detection for incidents impacting PII.

- Data retention & logging: We need to limit request/response retention to 14 days for production traffic and ensure logs can be purged on demand. Is that configurable for Hosted API customers under a contractual amendment?

We may propose redlines on processor obligations and breach notice timing depending on your answers. Also, please send the subprocessors CSV with hosting region for each vendor.

Thanks — can Marissa confirm? I'd prefer a short call Monday morning to align.

- Lydia
Senior Security Program Manager | Acme Payments

Hi all — thanks for looping me in, Ben. Quick legal/security responses below — happy to hop on a short call Monday if helpful.

1) Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard position is processor only. We do not claim joint-controller status for customer payloads or derived outputs in the DPA. For aggregated telemetry (non-PII, fully anonymized usage metrics) Redwood acts as an independent controller for internal product analytics; this is explicitly excluded from the customer data scope in Section 3 of the DPA. We will add a clarifying paragraph if helpful.

2) Subprocessors & regions: Attached CSV updated with hosting region for each vendor (EU/US/APAC). We do use a small number of US-based analytics providers who receive aggregated telemetry only; they do not receive raw customer request/response payloads. For subprocessors that might access logs for debugging we can mark them as "restricted" and notify Acme in advance.

3) Breach notice: Our policy is 72 hours from confirmation; confirmation requires initial triage and verification of scope. That said, we can commit to an interim notification within 24 hours from detection for incidents that may impact PII, followed by a full confirmed notice within 72 hours. We can add language to the DPA to reflect this two-step approach.

4) Retention & purge: For Hosted API customers the default 30-day retention is standard; however, for enterprise accounts (and on Dedicated) we can offer a contractual amendment that restricts request/response retention to 14 days and provides an on-demand purge process. For Hosted self-serve accounts this is not currently configurable.

Suggested next steps:
- Ben: propose a short call Mon 10am PT with Lydia + Tom + Marissa + Dev to walk the subprocessors list and agree on breach notice language.
- I'll prepare DPA language snippets for: 24-hour interim notice, 14-day retention amendment, and restricted-subprocessor flagging.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
